description: The bar chart illustrates the number of datasets related to hateful communication, categorized by year from 2012 to 2022, with a focus on the number of datasets per language. The vertical axis, labeled "Number of datasets," uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10 to 100, while the horizontal axis represents the years. The chart shows a general upward trend in the number of datasets over time, with a significant increase starting from 2016. In 2012 and 2013, the number of datasets is low, with only one dataset each year. From 2014 to 2015, the number of datasets remains at one. In 2016, the number of datasets increases to 10. In 2017, the number of datasets increases to 20, with 10 datasets in blue and 10 in orange. In 2018, the number of datasets increases to 30, with 20 datasets in blue and 10 in orange. In 2019, the number of datasets increases to 40, with 30 datasets in blue and 10 in orange. In 2020, the number of datasets increases to 50, with 40 datasets in blue and 10 in orange. In 2021, the number of datasets increases to 60, with 50 datasets in blue and 10 in orange. In 2022, the number of datasets increases to 70, with 60 datasets in blue and 10 in orange. The legend indicates that the blue bars represent datasets in language 1, the orange bars represent datasets in language 2, and the gray bars represent datasets in language 3. The chart shows that the number of datasets in language 1 has increased significantly over the years, while the number of datasets in language 2 and language 3 has remained relatively low.
